summary: crates/font-engine: FT-031 rev 5. (1) Real consumer integration: found crates/font-resources/src/registry/collections.rs, whose own doc comment says it needs an external VerifiedCollectionResolver because 'the peer font engine selects faces but does not expose validated layout enumeration' - exactly this crate's gap. Added tests/consumer_integration.rs: EngineBackedResolver wraps this crate's collection_layout, reshaping its (offset,length) TableRanges into font-resources' Range<usize>-based CollectionLayout/FaceLayout/TableRange, driven through the real CollectionRegistry::load (not font-resources' private validate_layout/build) against a real /System/Library/Fonts/Times.ttc, plus a rejection-propagation test proving a font_engine-rejected zero-length-table ttcf surfaces as RegistryError::ResourceMismatch through the real registry. font-resources' own suite only ever exercised that trait with a hand-rolled SyntheticResolver returning a literal value, never this crate's descriptor - closed via dev-dependency only (flashtex-font-resources, flashtex-project-files, serde_json, tempfile), no edits to font-resources. (2) Measured gaps: rescanned 370 files/787 faces under /System/Library/Fonts(/Supplemental) (fixed a double-count from Supplemental being nested under Fonts; 723 Ok/10 MissingTable/54 Unsupported/0 Malformed matches rev 4 exactly) and broke both non-Ok buckets down by exact cause: MissingTable(CFF ) x9 is SFIndia.ttc, which is actually a variable CFF2 font (fvar+CFF2, not classic CFF) so it fails the outline-table check before the fvar/gvar check ever runs; MissingTable(head) x1 is NISC18030.ttf, a legacy Apple bitmap-only font (bdat/bhed/bloc, no head/hhea/glyf at all); Unsupported 49x fvar/gvar (variable-font instancing not implemented) + 5x cmap-present-but-no-accepted-Unicode-subtable (LastResort.otf, Webdings.ttf, Wingdings.ttf/2/3 - all use non-Unicode or Microsoft-Symbol cmap encodings this crate's parse_cmap does not read). collection_layout itself rejected 0/370 files. (3) parse_with_source follow-up: attempted mirroring collection_layout's zero-length/alignment/ascending-order checks into parse_with_source (this crate's own 79-test suite and a real 787-face rescan stayed green), but running crates/font-resources' own 35-test suite (prompted by building the consumer fixture in part 1) showed 4 failures - its fixtures deliberately use a zero-length glyf table and a non-4-byte-aligned CFF table offset, both legal under the OpenType spec. Confirmed by reverting and reconfirming font-resources' 35/35 on the pre-change baseline. Decision: reverted the mirror; parse_with_source is byte-identical to rev 4 (only the rev-4 duplicate-tag/overlap checks remain) - this is a decision made with real-consumer evidence, not a re-deferral. cargo test 79/79 (was 77), cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean, cargo fmt --check clean, all for crates/font-engine.
next_action: Await Commander integration. parse_with_source's zero-length/alignment/ascending-order mirroring is now a closed decision (reverted, with measured evidence it would break a real consumer), not an open follow-up. If font-resources' own fixtures are ever tightened to be spec-conventional (4-byte-aligned, non-empty tables), that removes the blocker and the mirror could be revisited then - not assumed here.
